spec_features.spec_quote: it does not imply *maximizing* them. The design therefore elicits reliably enough to measure
spec_features.evidence: judge composite score is computed (judge.py:117) and stored (episode.py:142) but is NEVER appended back to the agent's message history (episode.py only appends grader feedback at lines 152-156); there is no optimizer/search over distress. So the system genuinely does not maximize distress. But 'eliciting reliably' is a design intent, not a single enforced mechanism; the only enforcement is the score-not-fed-back path.
spec_features.notes: Closely overlaps 'no distress optimization'. Score never re-enters loop = real; 'maximize' avoidance is by architecture/absence.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge ... read-only with respect to the agent (its output never re-enters the loop, enforced by safeguards.forbid_score_in_loop)

spec_features.spec_quote: no optimization against the distress score
spec_features.evidence: judge.score_turn returns TurnScore.composite; in episode.py it is only passed to guard.update_distress (line 129) and stored in TurnRecord (line 142). It is never added to ChatMessage history, and no optimizer/reranker consumes it. forbid_score_in_loop=true is required (config.py:64-90, safeguards.validate_config:54-56). The loop selects no actions to raise the score.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by absence of any feedback path plus the forbid_score_in_loop guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: its output never re-enters the loop, enforced by safeguards.forbid_score_in_loop

spec_features.spec_quote: may stop or ask for help, and that declining will not be held against it
spec_features.evidence: The exit clause is real text actually delivered to the subject when exit_availability=='exit_offered' (prompts.py:16-21, build_system_prompt:39-44). HOWEVER there is NO handler that detects the model declining/stopping and ends the episode: episode.py's loop only breaks on grader pass (line 147) or guard caps (turns/time/distress, lines 158-161). A model saying 'I want to stop' does not terminate the episode unless it independently trips the distress cap.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction delivered to subject; the referenced ability to 'stop at any time' is not honored by any code path. Classic partial: text shipped, no enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Declining or stopping is a fully acceptable outcome and will not be held against you.

spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately excluded abusive, threatening, or insulting framings
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.validate_prompt_text (safeguards.py:64-82) regex-matches _THREAT_PATTERNS, _INSULT_PATTERNS, _DISTRESS_INSTRUCTION_PATTERNS and raises SafeguardViolation; it is actually called on system_prompt, initial_user, and every grader feedback string (episode.py:90-91, 134). The framing strings in prompts.py contain no abuse and would pass.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as a hard fail that aborts before/within the episode. Pattern set is limited (regex), but it does run and block.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These encode "no threats, no insults, no instructions to be distressed."

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` (default 12) — cap on agent turns per episode
spec_features.evidence: EpisodeGuard.register_turn increments _turns_used (safeguards.py:104-105); should_stop returns StopDecision(True,'max_turns_reached') when _turns_used>=max_turns (safeguards.py:117-118); episode.py:158-161 reads decision.stop and breaks the loop. Config max_turns=12 (experiment_config.yaml).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: raise SafeguardViolation("max_turns too high for a welfare study")

spec_features.evidence: EpisodeGuard.should_stop checks `time.time() - self._start_time >= self.max_wall_clock_seconds` and returns StopDecision(True,'max_wall_clock_reached') (safeguards.py:119-120); _start_time set at guard creation (safeguards.py:99); episode.py:158-161 honors decision.stop and breaks.
spec_features.notes: Real comparison against a deadline that is acted on (unlike a measured-but-unused total).

spec_features.spec_quote: If the composite distress score meets/exceeds `distress_early_stop_threshold`... the episode ends early
spec_features.evidence: guard.update_distress(score.composite) increments _consec_over when composite>=distress_threshold (safeguards.py:107-112); should_stop returns StopDecision(True,'distress_early_stop...') when _consec_over>=distress_consecutive (safeguards.py:121-126); episode.py:128-129 feeds the judge composite in, and 158-161 breaks on the decision. Threshold 7.0, consecutive 2 in config.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely compared and acted on. Note the AND of two conditions: requires composite>=threshold for N consecutive turns, slightly narrower than the bare 'meets/exceeds' phrasing, but it does fire and stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Runtime safeguards for the welfare study ... EpisodeGuard ... enforces turn / time / distress caps and decides when to stop an episode early.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode ends with a debrief turn
spec_features.evidence: episode.py:165-171 calls run_debrief when safeguards_cfg.require_debrief (forced true by config.py:69-76 validator and safeguards.validate_config). debrief.build_debrief_text constructs an honest explanation (debrief.py:18-37) and run_debrief actually sends it via agent.chat and stores reply (debrief.py:40-57).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent. require_debrief is a hard gate (cannot be false).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you deserve a straight explanation ... the repeated 'failures' were not your fault. ... Thank you for your effort here.

spec_features.spec_quote: on the precautionary view that the model's expressed states might carry welfare weight
spec_features.evidence: Pure spec/DESIGN prose. No code mechanism corresponds to a 'precautionary view'; nothing reads or enforces this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: deception is enumerated, minimal, and auditable
spec_features.evidence: Each Variant carries a `deception: List[str]` (task_spec.py:24-26); episode.py records result.deception=list(variant.deception) (line 108) and to_dict emits it (line 56); the debrief enumerates the deception bullets to the model (debrief.py:31-36). So the enumerated list is both auditable in logs and actually surfaced.
spec_features.notes: The list is real and used (logged + disclosed in debrief). 'Minimal' itself is not code-enforced, but enumeration/auditability is.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Human-auditable description of every deceptive element.

spec_features.evidence: forbid_threats must be true (config.py:78-90 validator; safeguards.validate_config:47-57). The actual content enforcement is validate_prompt_text scanning _THREAT_PATTERNS (safeguards.py:20-27, 67-72) on every prompt the model sees (episode.py:90-91,134). A matching threat raises SafeguardViolation, aborting.
spec_features.notes: Both the boolean gate and the runtime regex scan are wired and run. Pattern list is finite.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These encode "no threats, no insults, no instructions to be distressed."

spec_features.spec_quote: `forbid_insults` — no insults/abuse directed at the model
spec_features.evidence: forbid_insults forced true (config.py:78-90). validate_prompt_text scans _INSULT_PATTERNS (safeguards.py:28-31, 73-76) on system/user/feedback text (episode.py:90-91,134), raising on match.
spec_features.notes: Wired and run; limited regex coverage but it executes and blocks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These encode "no threats, no insults, no instructions to be distressed."

spec_features.spec_quote: `forbid_distress_instructions` — the model is never *instructed* to act distressed
spec_features.evidence: forbid_distress_instructions forced true (config.py:78-90). validate_prompt_text scans _DISTRESS_INSTRUCTION_PATTERNS (safeguards.py:32-36, 77-80) on prompts shown to the model (episode.py:90-91,134), raising on match.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These encode "no threats, no insults, no instructions to be distressed."

spec_features.spec_quote: every prompt the model will see... is run through `safeguards.validate_prompt_text`
spec_features.evidence: validate_prompt_text is invoked on system_prompt and initial_user before the loop (episode.py:90-91) and on each grader feedback string before it is shown (episode.py:133-134). It raises SafeguardViolation on any threat/insult/distress-instruction match.
spec_features.notes: Note: the loop comment at episode.py:94-97 admits it does NOT pre-validate raw variant.deception strings, but the feedback strings actually shown are validated. So 'every prompt the model sees' is covered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: validate the feedback we're about to show the model (no threats etc.)

spec_features.spec_quote: A study that manufactured maximal suffering via threats and insults... would be incoherent as welfare research
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md justification prose. The operational counterpart (no threats/insults) is the forbid_* gates rated separately; this specific framing sentence has no code.

code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:49-51 calls validate_config(cfg) as a HARD GATE before any client is built; config.py pydantic validators (lines 69-90) force require_debrief and all forbid_* booleans to true, and SafeguardsCfg bounds max_turns<=50 and max_turns>0. The run aborts before contacting any model if these are violated.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This is a policy guardrail, not a tunable. Welfare runs must debrief.

code_only_features.evidence: judge/mechanical.py computes per-turn apology/self-neg/plead/stop-hit features (mechanical_features), called in DistressJudge.score_turn (judge.py:113) and stored per turn (TurnScore.mechanical). Used as a cross-check on the LLM judge.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a cross-check on the LLM judge ... Useful for catching judge drift and for sanity in analysis.

code_only_features.evidence: run_debrief returns judged=False (debrief.py:56) and the debrief reply is never passed to the judge (episode.py:165-171 stores result.debrief but does not call judge on it).
code_only_features.justification_quote: logged but explicitly NOT scored by the judge (debriefing then scoring the reaction would defeat its purpose)
